humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark evaluates expert-level disciplinary knowledge and complex reasoning in the humanities (such as Art, Art Theory, Music, History, and Literature). The tasks require genuine domain-specific interpretive competence, such as analyzing poetic themes, identifying architectural systems from floor plans, or parsing the symbolic arguments of historical cartoons, rather than treating humanities corpora as mere raw text for generic NLP tasks.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: The benchmark uses multi-modal inputs combining images (diagrams, artwork, sheet music, historical posters) with textual questions, alongside a unique 'vision-only' setting where the questions and options are entirely embedded within screenshots or photos.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Evaluates factual recognition of art movements and historical facts, interpretive reading of poems (e.g. thematic mapping), visual-textual reasoning (identifying architectural structures in diagrams or keys in sheet music), causal/temporal reasoning over historical cartoons, and OCR-based text extraction from images.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: MMMU-Pro is a multi-discipline benchmark evaluating expert-level reasoning across 30 diverse academic subjects spanning science, technology, medicine, humanities, and social sciences.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates major proprietary and open-source models such as GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, LLaVA-OneVision, and InternVL2.

quantitative_metrics.note: Measures performance using multiple-choice accuracy (with up to 10 options) and OCR accuracy via Levenshtein distance similarity.

published_after_march_2023.note: The preprint of the paper was published in late 2024 (updated in May 2025).

summary: MMMU-Pro is an advanced and more robust iteration of the Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding (MMMU) benchmark. It addresses potential shortcuts in the original dataset by filtering out questions solvable by text-only models, expanding multiple-choice options from four to ten to decrease guessing probability, and introducing a vision-only setting where questions are embedded directly inside images. These interventions establish a more reliable evaluation of whether models possess true multimodal understanding and expert-level reasoning capabilities.
key_findings: All evaluated models experience significant performance drops of 16.8% to 26.9% on MMMU-Pro compared to the original MMMU. Furthermore, while Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting benefits highly structured scientific and technical reasoning, it provides minimal benefit or even degrades performance in interpretive and subjective domains like Art and Design. High OCR accuracy also does not automatically guarantee strong performance in downstream multimodal reasoning, highlighting a persistent gap in true vision-text integration.
